label: Energy Objects
desc: Objects producing, converting, storing, or distributing energy: generators, turbines, batteries, inverters, and the dams and grids that carry their output.

label: Energy good producer
desc: Transforms energy into delivered power, force, or conditioned energy — the producing technical element whose delivered good is energy.

label: Primary generation
desc: Plants that convert a primary resource — falling water, radiation, wind — into electrical energy.

label: Three Gorges Dam
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Energy Technology → Production Technical System → Generation System → Production Technical Object → Three Gorges Dam
desc: Hydroelectric generating dam in the Yangtze basin: concrete barrier, spillway, ship lift and a turbine hall of 32 units. Typed `Production Technical Object` inside `Generation System`; the corpus decomposition gives the dam body and turbine hall, not its economics — that is the good taxonomy's job.

label: Stationary storage
desc: Objects that hold energy for later delivery: electrochemical banks, pumped-hydro reservoirs, and the inverters that couple them to the grid.

label: Battery Bank
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Stationary Energy Storage → Constitutive Technical Object → Battery Bank
desc: The electrochemical store at the heart of a stationary installation: cell stacks, modules and racks whose operative structure is the reversible reaction. Constitutive of the installed system, traded as lithium-ion accumulators.

label: Material Objects
desc: Objects whose identity is their substance: alloys, ceramics, polymers, raw materials and the minerals they are won from. Generally `Constitutive Technical Object` — they constitute larger objects rather than acting.

label: Constitutive object
desc: Component or constituent constituting a larger technical object or system — the stuff-kind of production, not a producer and not a support.

label: Metals & alloys
desc: Material families won from ore and refined by smelting, then traded as grade.

label: Steel
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Material → Technical Resource → Technical Abiogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Steel
desc: The iron-carbon alloy family, classified by composition, microstructure, treatment and use — A36 and 1018 for construction, 4140 low-alloy, 304 stainless, DP600 auto sheet, M2 and D2 tool steel. A stuff-kind: it constitutes structures, machines and tools.

label: Rare Earth Elements
atlas: Technical Element → Constitutive Technical Object → Rare Earth Elements
desc: The lanthanide family separated from monazite and bastnäsite and embedded as NdFeB magnets, phosphors and catalysts. A raw-material object whose value is almost entirely downstream.

label: Ceramics & glass
desc: Non-metallic mineral material families fired or melted into a finished substance.

label: Portland Cement
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Abiogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Portland Cement
desc: Calcium-silicate clinker ground with gypsum — the binder that, with aggregate and water, constitutes concrete. The classic intermediate object: never used as such, always consumed into something else.

label: Float Glass
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Abiogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Float Glass
desc: Glass cast on a molten-tin bath into a flat, fire-polished sheet — the substrate of windows, displays and solar modules.

label: Semiconductor materials
desc: Single-crystal substrates and wide-bandgap compounds whose materiality is a controlled defect structure.

label: Silicon Wafer
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Abiogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Silicon Wafer
desc: A sliced, lapped and polished single-crystal silicon disc — the substrate every integrated circuit is built on. Untyped by function, typed by purity.

label: SiC Wafer
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Material Technology Set → Constitutive Technical Object → SiC Wafer
desc: Silicon-carbide substrate for power and RF devices: a wide-bandgap material that survives electric fields silicon cannot.

label: Semiconductor compounds
desc: Compound crystals that are the active medium of a device rather than a substrate under it.

label: Gallium Nitride
atlas: Technical Element → Constitutive Technical Object → Gallium Nitride
desc: A III–V wide-bandgap compound: the gain medium of blue LEDs and the channel of fast, high-voltage power transistors. Its materiality is the product.

label: Polymers & bioplastics
desc: Long-chain material families — petroleum-derived or fermented — formed into parts by extrusion and moulding.

label: Petroleum Polymer
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Material → Constitutive Technical Object → Petroleum Polymer
desc: Polymer resin grades — PE, PP, PS, PVC, PET — sold as pellets and melt-formed into parts. The material of choice wherever a part must be cheap and shaped in one shot.

label: Bioplastic
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Biogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Bioplastic
desc: Fermented or crop-derived polymer resin — PLA, PHA — with the same forming behaviour as a petroleum polymer and a different end-of-life story.

label: Biogenic materials
desc: Material families grown rather than won: timber, fibre, leather.

label: Lumber
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Resource → Technical Biogenic Material Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Lumber
desc: Sawn and graded timber — the structural material of frame construction and the raw stock of furniture and formwork.

label: Machinery & Machine Elements
desc: Objects that do mechanical work or transmit it: producing machines, machine tools, drives, gearing, bearings and the couplings between them.

label: Machine
desc: Drive, motion, or power package that actuates a tool or equipment — the guide's `Machine` support kind, used here where the object's identity is the motion it generates.

label: Driving machinery
desc: Prime movers and drive packages that turn fuel, electricity or fluid into shaft work.

label: Motor Shop
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Appliance Production → Production Technical Object → Motor Shop
desc: The electric-motor line of an appliance plant: stator winding, rotor stacking, magnet insertion and test — the drive package the finished appliance is built around.

label: Transmission elements
desc: Elements that carry, reduce or redirect motion between a machine and what it drives.

label: Gear Train
atlas: Technical Element → General Technique → Mechanical System → Constitutive Technical Object → Gear Train
desc: A meshed set of toothed wheels fixing the ratio between input and output shaft — the canonical machine element from the corpus's `Mechanical System` decomposition.

label: Bearing Set
atlas: Technical Element → General Technique → Mechanical System → Constitutive Technical Object → Bearing Set
desc: Rolling or plain bearing elements that constrain a rotating shaft while carrying its load — the element that decides a machine's life.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — formed, shaped, treated, or relocated matter whose finished state is the output.

label: Machine tools
desc: Machines whose product is a machined surface: a lathe, a mill, a drill press, a grinder.

label: Lathe Bed
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Machine Tool Production → Production Technical Object → Lathe Bed
desc: The cast bed that carries the headstock, saddle and tailstock of a lathe — the object that fixes the straightness of everything machined on it.

label: CNC machining cell
desc: A numerically controlled machine tool with its fixture, tool magazine and post-processor: the object whose output is a tolerance rather than a shape.

label: Production facility
desc: Built structure or site that houses, protects, and services production — read here as the works in which machines are installed.

label: Manufacturing works
desc: Industrial buildings: machine halls, foundries, mills — the shell a production line is set into.

label: Machine Hall
desc: The long-span, crane-served hall in which machine tools and lines are installed — structure, foundation block and power drop treated as one object.

label: Tools & Instruments
desc: Implements that bear on the workpiece or measure the process: hand and power tools, cutting tools, gauges, sensors and laboratory apparatus.

label: Support — tool
desc: Implement that bears directly on the workpiece or target, shaping, holding, cutting, or joining it.

label: Hand & power tools
desc: Held implements driven by the hand or by a small integral motor.

label: Hand power tool line
desc: The manufactured class of corded and cordless tools — drill, grinder, saw — assembled on a shared motor-and-switch platform.

label: Support — instrument
desc: Implement that measures, indicates, regulates, or monitors a production variable.

label: Metrology instruments
desc: Instruments whose reading is a length, an angle or a shape.

label: Coordinate Measuring Machine
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Metrology Services Set → Production Technical Object → Coordinate Measuring Machine
desc: A granite-and-air-bearing bridge that touches a part at sampled points and reports coordinates — the instrument that arbitrates whether the machine that made it was right.

label: Sensors & probes
desc: Instruments that transduce a physical variable into a signal a controller can read.

label: Process Sensor
guide: Constitutive Technical Object, readable as Technical Element of a measurement chain
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Biotechnology → Production Technical System → Upstream → Constitutive Technical Object → Sensor
desc: pH, dissolved-oxygen, CO₂ and temperature probes in a production line: constitutive of the control loop, and the element whose drift silently invalidates a batch.

label: Construction & Built Works
desc: Objects built in place out of earth, concrete, steel and masonry: structures, foundations, earth-retaining works, tunnels and the plant that raises them.

label: Support — facility
desc: Built structure or site that houses, protects, and services production — here the works that carry, protect or service other activity.

label: Earthworks & retaining
desc: Works whose material is the ground itself, placed or held back.

label: Retaining Wall
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Practice → Geotechnical Engineering → Production Technical System → Geotechnical Construction Site → Production Technical Object → Retaining Wall
desc: A structure that holds a soil mass at a different elevation on its two faces. Its constitution includes a natural element — the retained soil — which is why it is typed as an object of the geotechnical site, not of a factory.

label: Embankment
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Practice → Geotechnical Engineering → Production Technical System → Geotechnical Construction Site → Production Technical Object → Embankment
desc: A raised earth structure carrying a road, rail line or water — compacted fill whose stability is a slope-stability, not a strength-of-material, question.

label: Foundation
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Practice → Geotechnical Engineering → Production Technical System → Geotechnical Construction Site → Production Technical Object → Foundation
desc: The deep or shallow element that transfers a structure's load into the ground — a facility in the guide's sense, since it merely holds what it carries.

label: Tunnel Lining
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Practice → Geotechnical Engineering → Production Technical System → Geotechnical Construction Site → Production Technical Object → Tunnel Lining
desc: Segmental or cast-in-place support lining an excavated tunnel against the ground it passes through — the structure that makes an opening permanent.

label: Buildings & envelopes
desc: Enclosed works: housing, halls, containers for people and production.

label: House
desc: The dwelling as a technical object: envelope, structure, services and interior environment — an assembly whose operative behaviour is shelter, not transformation.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here the site plant that builds works out of raw site conditions.

label: Site plant
desc: Machines deployed on a construction site to lift, place, compact or excavate.

label: Tower Crane
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Construction Technology Set → Production Technical Object → Tower Crane
desc: A vertical mast with a rotating jib that raises materials through a building's height — a producer in the narrow sense that it relocates matter, and a support in the guide's sense that it transforms nothing itself.

label: Transport Objects
desc: Objects that relocate goods and people: vehicles, vessels, rolling stock, aircraft, drones and the conveyor systems that move matter inside a plant.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here the located matter, since transport's output is a change of place.

label: Road & rail vehicles
desc: Self-propelled and towed objects that move on a road or a track.

label: Automobile
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Automobile System
desc: A road vehicle as a production technical system: body, powertrain, chassis, electrical architecture and the assembly line that constitutes it.

label: Vessels
desc: Floating objects built to carry cargo or perform work at sea.

label: Hull Structure
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Naval Shipbuilding → Constitutive Technical Object → Hull Structure
desc: The welded steel shell, decks and bulkheads of a vessel — the object whose fabrication is the shipyard's whole craft.

label: Aerial objects
desc: Objects that displace themselves and their payload through the air.

label: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
desc: An airframe with flight controller, propulsion and payload whose production work is surveying, spraying or inspection rather than carriage.

label: Support — equipment
desc: Apparatus that conveys, holds, positions, or otherwise enables production without transforming the delivered good.

label: Conveying systems
desc: Equipment that carries material between stations of a process.

label: Conveyor Line
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Industrial Machinery → Production Technical Object → Conveyor Line
desc: A belt or roller track linking stations of a line. Inside a bottling plant it transforms nothing and produces nothing — the guide's textbook demotion from producer to `Production Equipment` support.

label: Chemical & Process Objects
desc: Objects whose operation is a chemical or physical transformation carried out in vessels, columns, reactors and the piping that joins them.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here by reaction, separation or formulation rather than by shaping.

label: Reaction vessels
desc: Objects that hold a reacting mixture and control its temperature and agitation.

label: Reactor Train
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Basic Chemicals Production → Production Technical Object → Reactor Train
desc: A cascade of reactors and heat exchangers carrying a reaction to conversion — the train, not the vessel, is the producing object.

label: Bioreactor
desc: A stirred, sparged, jacketed vessel in which cells grow: agitator, sparger and the probes that hold pH and dissolved oxygen. Stainless or single-use, the object is the same.

label: Separation equipment
desc: Objects that split a mixture into its components by boiling point, solubility or size.

label: Distillation Column
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Basic Chemicals Production → Production Technical Object → Distillation Column
desc: A vertical shell of trays or packing in which rising vapour and falling liquid exchange and split by volatility.

label: Support — equipment
desc: Apparatus that conveys, holds, positions, or otherwise enables production without transforming the delivered good — here the piping and valving of a plant.

label: Piping & valving
desc: The static equipment that routes and stops flow between vessels.

label: Valve Assembly
atlas: Technical Element → General Technique → Mechanical System → Constitutive Technical Object → Valve Assembly
desc: Body, trim, stem and actuator forming one controllable flow restriction — the smallest object of a plant that can be said to decide anything.

label: Electronics & Computing
desc: Objects whose operation is electrical or computational: devices, components, boards, hardware platforms and the virtual objects software constitutes.

label: Constitutive object
desc: Component or constituent constituting a larger technical object — here the devices soldered into a board or a module.

label: Discrete devices
desc: Single-function semiconductor and passive devices.

label: Transistor
atlas: Technical Element → Constitutive Technical Object → Transistor
desc: A three-terminal switch and amplifier — the element every digital object is composed of, and the corpus's canonical case of a constitutive object.

label: IGBT Module
atlas: Technical Element → Constitutive Technical Object → Transistor → Constitutive Technical Object → IGBT Module
desc: Insulated-gate bipolar switches packaged with their diode and driver — the device that lets an inverter move kilowatts.

label: Boards & modules
desc: Assemblies that mount devices on a substrate and provide their interconnect.

label: Electrical Board
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → House System → Constitutive Technical Object → Electrical Board
desc: A populated board — passive components, devices and connectors on the interconnect that binds them into a circuit.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here the fabricated wafer and the assembled device.

label: Semiconductor fabrication
desc: The process objects that turn a substrate into finished devices.

label: Lithography Cell
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Semiconductor Fabrication → Production Technical Object → Lithography Cell
desc: Scanner, track and metrology bound into one cell that prints a layer of a wafer — the tool whose resolution sets what a node means.

label: Production technical system
desc: A system producing or operating technical objects — objects that are only meaningful as an integrated whole of parts.

label: Computing platforms
desc: Finished computing objects sold as such.

label: Smartphone
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Electronics Technology Set → Production Technical Object → Smartphone
desc: Radio, application processor, display and battery in a sealed case — the technical object that the goods taxonomy also lists as a consumer product, which is exactly the overlap the two catalogues exist to show.

label: Wi-Fi Router
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Electronics Technology Set → Production Technical Object → Wi-Fi Router
desc: An embedded switch, radio and forwarding engine — a technical object whose behaviour is almost entirely its firmware.

label: Virtual object
desc: A technical object whose operative structure is primarily informational or computational and whose operation is realized through computation.

label: Runtime platforms
desc: Software whose operative structure is a deployable runtime: a scheduler, an application server, a cache.

label: JobRunr
atlas: Technical Element → Constitutive Technical Object → JobRunr
desc: A JVM background-job scheduler distributed as a library: dashboards, queues, a recurring-job store. The corpus's clearest virtual technical object — no mass, one behaviour.

label: WildFly
desc: A Jakarta EE application server: an object assembled from a core, extension modules, a deployment repository and an Undertow listener.

label: Trained models
desc: Computational objects whose value is their parameters, not their code.

label: Transformer Model
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Transformer System → Production Technical Object → Transformer Model
desc: A stack of attention and feed-forward sublayers with learned weights — a virtual object whose identity is a checkpoint and a tokenizer.

label: Food & Agricultural Objects
desc: Objects of field, barn, greenhouse and processing plant: machinery, housing, stores and the processing lines that turn harvest and herd into food.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here cultivated biomass and processed food.

label: Field machinery
desc: Machines deployed on open land to sow, tend and harvest.

label: Combine Harvester
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Plant Cultivation Technical Domain Set → Technical Element Set → Field Operations And Mechanization Set → Production Technical Object → Combine Harvester
desc: A self-propelled machine that cuts, threshes and winnows grain in one pass — three classical operations fused into a single producing object.

label: Processing lines
desc: Lines that convert raw harvest or milk into a storable, traded food.

label: Pasteurization Line
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Dairy Production → Production Technical Object → Pasteurization Line
desc: Heat exchanger, holding tube, cooler and valves that take raw milk through a time–temperature kill step.

label: Bottling Line
desc: Washer, filler, capper and labeller synchronized by accumulation conveyors — the line as one producing object, every conveyor in it a support.

label: Support — facility
desc: Built structure or site that houses, protects, and services production — here housing, greenhouses, barns and stores.

label: Animal housing
desc: Built environments that shelter and service livestock.

label: Barn & Housing Structure
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Animal Husbandry Technical Set → Production Technical Object → Barn And Housing Structure
desc: The shed, ventilation and restraint system that shelters a herd — a facility whose environment is the production variable.

label: Controlled environments
desc: Enclosed growing or storing environments where climate is engineered.

label: Greenhouse
desc: A glazed or film-clad envelope with heating, venting and fertigation — a building whose whole point is to be a controlled environment.

label: Medical & Laboratory Objects
desc: Objects that act on patients or on samples: instruments, diagnostic devices, implants and the laboratory apparatus that makes evidence.

label: Service good producer
desc: Transforms reality by performing a service on entities, patients, or stocks, where the performed service *is* the good.

label: Diagnostic instruments
desc: Instruments that convert a sample or a body into a recorded signal.

label: Sequencing Instrument
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Plant Health Technical Set → Technical Element Set → Diagnostic And Detection Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Sequencing Instrument
desc: A fluidic, optical and computational object that reads a DNA strand base by base — a producer whose delivered good is information.

label: Electron Microscope
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Laboratory Tooling Set → Production Technical Object → Electron Microscope
desc: Column, lenses, specimen stage and detectors forming one instrument that turns an electron beam into an image of a surface.

label: Constitutive object
desc: Component or constituent constituting a larger technical object — here the material installed inside a body.

label: Implant materials
desc: Biomaterials that constitute a device remaining in the body.

label: Titanium Implant
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Material Technology Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Titanium Implant
desc: A machined titanium body — screw, plate, joint — whose constitutive material is chosen for biocompatibility as much as strength.

label: Support — instrument
desc: Implement that measures, indicates, regulates, or monitors a production variable — here the bench apparatus of a clinical or QC lab.

label: Laboratory apparatus
desc: Bench instruments that condition, separate or read a sample.

label: Thermocycler
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Plant Health Technical Set → Technical Element Set → Diagnostic And Detection Set → Constitutive Technical Object → Thermocycler
desc: A heated block and lid that drive a PCR reaction through cycles of temperature — the instrument that made molecular biology a routine.

label: Water & Environmental Works
desc: Objects that supply, move, store, treat or dispose of water and waste: pumping sets, treatment trains, dams and irrigation assemblies.

label: Material good producer
desc: Transforms matter into a delivered material good — here potable water and treated effluent.

label: Irrigation & water supply
desc: Objects that move water to where it is needed.

label: Drip Irrigation Assembly
atlas: Technical Element → Technical Element Set → Plant Cultivation Technical Domain Set → Technical Element Set → Water And Irrigation Set → Production Technical Object → Drip Irrigation Assembly
desc: Headworks, filter, mainline and emitters delivering metered water to roots — equipment that conveys rather than transforms.

label: Pumping & fluid handling
desc: Machines that add head and flow to a liquid.

label: Pump
desc: A casing and impeller (or a reciprocating chamber) that converts shaft work into fluid head. The corpus decomposes it inside every plant it serves; it stands here as its own object.

label: Support — facility
desc: Built structure or site that houses, protects, and services production — here the works that contain water.

label: Containment works
desc: Civil works built to hold or contain water and residue.

label: Tailings Facility
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Mining System → Production Technical Object → Tailings Facility
desc: A dammed impoundment for mine residue — a work whose retained material is the hazard, and whose failure mode is the design question.

label: Facilities & Infrastructure
desc: Objects whose product is the service a place provides: logistics hubs, warehouses, terminals, retail and service premises.

label: Support — facility
desc: Built structure or site that houses, protects, and services production.

label: Logistics & storage
desc: Premises where goods are held, sorted or transferred rather than made.

label: Cold Store
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Dairy Production → Production Technical Object → Cold Store
desc: An insulated envelope with refrigeration plant, evaporators and monitoring — a facility whose stored good is time.

label: Warehouse
desc: Racking, floor, dock and handling equipment forming one storage object — the node where goods stop being in transit.

label: Service premises
desc: Built objects whose product is a hospitality, retail or maintenance service.

label: Hotel Property
atlas: Technical Element → Production Technical System → Tourism System → Production Technical Object → Hotel Property
desc: Rooms, plant and front-of-house systems as one facility — a technical object whose delivered good is a stay.
